fs/watch#

FileWatch observes an existing file or directory without exposing blocking operating-system events through Cursor.

Version: v1.0.0

Synopsis#

let watch = FileWatch(path: workspace.path());
defer watch.close();
let event is FileEvent = await watch.event();
output.writeln(event::Change::kind.string(), ": ", event.path().string());

Description#

FileWatch observes an existing file or directory without exposing blocking operating-system events through Cursor. A directory watch covers the directory itself and its immediate children; it is deliberately not recursive. Use one FileWatch per directory when a tree must be observed.

Wait for one change:

Consume changes continuously:

let watch = FileWatch(path: configuration.parent());
defer watch.close();
loop {
    let event is FileEvent = await watch.event();
    if event.path() == configuration {
        reload(configuration);
    }
}

A rename carries the new path in path() and the old path in previous_path():

let event is FileEvent = await watch.event();
if event::Change::kind == FileEventKind.renamed {
    output.writeln(
        event.previous_path().string(),
        " -> ",
        event.path().string(),
    );
}

previous_path() is intentionally unavailable for created, modified and removed events. Only one event() call may be pending on a watch. Providers may coalesce repeated identical changes that happen faster than they can be observed, but preserve the order of the events they do report.
